correctness.rationale: The sixth-moment cumulants are exact. Hölder gives the sharp spike upper bound and even-dimensional lower bound. At any minimum a two-coordinate perturbation excludes zeros; stationarity and a strictly convex quartic equation give exactly one positive and one negative coefficient value. An exact rational-function derivative factors through the displayed cubic; its signs prove a unique minimizing ratio at every multiplicity, and a finite minimum over these gives the global lower endpoint. The connected sphere yields all intermediate ratios. The supplied checker independently reconstructs moments with a Bell recursion and confirms the derivative identity.

originality.rationale: The exact Poisson sixth cumulant identity is known; the proposed contribution is the unrestricted sharp real coefficient optimization, its all-nonzero two-level minimizers, its finite cubic endpoint prescription and parity-sensitive equality structure. The primary works inspected establish the stochastic framework, combinatorial moments, and nonsharp norm comparability but do not state the precise extremal classification. Historical coverage remains incomplete, hence bibliographic risk.
residual_risks: A specialized older or unindexed theorem may encode the same constrained optimization under a different description.
Only mathematically relevant portions, not every page, of the primary full texts were closely read; the originality assessment is correspondingly qualified.

value.rationale: Sharp L6/L2 embeddings and equality geometry of all finite-dimensional equal-intensity Poisson first-chaos spaces give a natural, reproducible norm invariant. The odd-dimensional nonflat two-level extremizers, in contrast with even-dimensional balanced flat directions, reflect genuine distributional asymmetry. The finite cubic prescription reduces the complete sharp problem to explicit algebraic quantities and removes the original continuous optimization without assuming an unsupported winner among multiplicities.
